cards.text: We're up north in Israel now. In the twenty-third year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu becomes king of Israel, and he reigns in Samaria seventeen years. Stay close, friend, because this chapter is a whole parade of kings with names that sound alike.

cards.question: True or false: King Jehoahaz turns away from the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat, an earlier king, had caused Israel to commit.

cards.text: So the anger of the LORD burns against Israel. Over and over, He hands them over to Hazael king of Aram, and then to his son Ben-hadad.

cards.question: Aram keeps crushing Israel. What does King Jehoahaz do?

answers.text: He seeks the favor of the LORD
He sends gold to King Hazael
He asks Egypt to send help

cards.question: The LORD listens to King Jehoahaz. Why does the text say He listens?

answers.text: He saw how Aram oppressed Israel

cards.question: The LORD answers. He gives Israel a ___, and they escape the power of the Arameans.

cards.text: Free from Aram, the people of Israel live in their own homes again, the way they did before. I bet it felt like my first day out of the junk drawer: ROOM. TO. STRETCH.

cards.question: True or false: Once they're rescued, Israel finally turns away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam.

cards.text: Nope, they keep walking in those same sins, and the Asherah pole even stays standing right there in Samaria. That's me getting pulled out of the junk drawer and asking, "Wait, can I go back in for a nap?"
Here's how bad things got for Jehoahaz. The king of Aram destroyed his army and made them like the dust at threshing.

cards.question: True or false: Aram leaves King Jehoahaz with only ten chariots.

cards.text: TEN chariots, fifty horsemen and ten thousand foot soldiers, and that's the WHOLE army. The rest of Jehoahaz's story is written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

cards.question: King Jehoahaz rests with his fathers. Where is he buried?
King Jehoahaz has died. Who reigns in his place?

cards.text: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz becomes king of Israel in Samaria, and he reigns sixteen years. Joash in Judah, Jehoash in Israel, same time, almost the same name: that's two guys named Mike in one group chat, and NOBODY knows who's replying.

cards.question: New king, new start? What does King Jehoash do in the sight of the LORD?

answers.text: Evil by walking in Jeroboam's sins
Right by tearing down the Asherah pole
Right by bringing Israel back to the LORD

cards.text: The rest of his story, including his war against Amaziah king of Judah, is written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel. Then Jehoash rests with his fathers and is buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
Then Jeroboam takes the throne. Not Jeroboam son of Nebat, friend. This one is Jehoash's own son (2 Kings 14:16), and that group chat just got ANOTHER guy named Mike.
Now the story steps back into the days of King Jehoash. Elisha, the prophet, has fallen sick with the illness he will die from, and Jehoash comes down to see him.

cards.question: King Jehoash stands beside the dying prophet Elisha. What does the king do?

answers.text: He asks Elisha to anoint him
He sits beside Elisha in silence

cards.text: He cries, "My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!" Then Elisha, sick in bed, tells the king to take a bow and some arrows, and the king does it.

cards.question: True or false: Elisha tells King Jehoash to put his hand on the bow, and then Elisha puts his own hands on the king's hands.

cards.text: Elisha tells him to open the east window. Then Elisha says, "Shoot!" and the king shoots.

cards.question: King Jehoash's arrow flies out the east window. What does Elisha say that arrow is?

answers.text: The LORD's arrow of victory over Aram
A sign that Elisha will be healed
A warning to the king of Judah

cards.question: Elisha says King Jehoash will strike the Arameans in Aphek. How far will the king take it?

answers.text: Until he has put an end to them
Until their king asks for peace

cards.text: Then Elisha says, "Take the arrows!" The king takes them, and Elisha says, "Strike the ground!"

cards.question: King Jehoash takes the arrows and strikes the ground ___ times, and then he stops.

cards.text: Elisha is angry and tells him he should have struck the ground five or six times, and then he would have struck down Aram until he had put an end to it. Three and done, friend? That's me stamping three cookies, untying my apron and calling it a batch.

cards.question: King Jehoash stopped at three. Now what does Elisha say the king will do to Aram?

answers.text: Strike down Aram only three times

cards.text: Then Elisha, the man of God, dies and is buried. I'm not crying, friend, that's just steam off the oven.
Now, raiders from Moab used to come into the land every spring. Once, while some Israelites are burying a man, they suddenly see a band of raiders.

cards.question: Raiders are coming, and these Israelites still have a body to bury. What do they do with it?
True or false: When the man's body touches the bones of Elisha, the man is revived and stands up on his feet.

cards.text: All through the reign of Jehoahaz, Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel. But the LORD is gracious to Israel, has compassion on them and turns toward them.

cards.question: The LORD has compassion on Israel and turns toward them. Why does the text say He does it?

answers.text: His covenant with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob
The sacrifices Israel offered at the altar
The promise Israel made to tear down idols

cards.text: And to this day, the LORD has been unwilling to destroy them or cast them from His presence. Then Hazael king of Aram dies, and his son Ben-hadad reigns in his place.

cards.question: Now King Jehoash gets his shot at Ben-hadad. Think back to those arrows on the ground. How many times does Jehoash defeat him?

cards.text: With those wins, Jehoash takes back the cities Hazael had taken in battle from his father Jehoahaz. Three strikes on the ground, three wins, just like Elisha said, and I bet that king wished he'd kept swinging those arrows.

findings.problem: The first choice card has no setup. Card 1 never says what kind of king Jehoahaz is. It never mentions that he did evil (v2), and it never brings up Jeroboam's sins. So whether he turns away from those sins is a coin flip. This is a reasoned point in the passage, not an unavoidable discovery question. A short setup line would let the baker reason it out without giving the answer away.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The joke's action doesn't match the fact. In v6, Israel keeps walking in the same sins after being rescued. In the joke, Papa Dorin asks to go back into the drawer, which is a different action: returning to captivity. It also changes his backstory. He was never 'pulled out' of the drawer. The drawer vanished after he said yes, and the joke makes him want to go back.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. Both wrong answers start with 'Right by...' and the only answer starting with 'Evil by...' is the odd one out. A baker can pick it by its shape alone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Then Jeroboam takes the throne.' / 'Not Jeroboam son of Nebat, friend.' / 'This one is Jehoash's own son...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: Elisha's anger and words, then 'Three and done, friend?', then 'That's me stamping three cookies...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. Seven of the 10 choice cards are multiple choice (cards 2, 6, 7, 11, 14, 17, 19). There are only 2 true or false cards and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
